title: Chapter 211: Scary Mannequins
html:
On the way, Chen Ge called the workshop owner. Assuming Chen Ge had changed his mind and agreed to help lonely customers everywhere, the man rushed from home before hearing an explanation. Chen Ge ate breakfast outside the workshop while he waited. The owner arrived within twenty minutes.

“Boss Qian, I need to borrow the workshop again. Money won’t be a problem.” It was not exactly a lie. Chen Ge had little money now, but he expected that to change.

“Why mention money the moment we meet? We’re old friends. Talking about payment cheapens the relationship.” The slightly overweight man sat beside Chen Ge. “Just leave me one of your mannequins.”

“Are you certain? My mannequins aren’t intended for that kind of use.” Boss Qian had treated him kindly, so Chen Ge did not want to deceive him. “I’ll make several new ones today. Decide after you see them.”

Boss Qian unlocked the glass door, then bowed three times before entering.

“What are you doing? Are you that afraid?” Chen Ge remembered that the boss did not have this habit when they first met.

“I don’t know. Ever since you made that first batch, I’ve felt something watching me from behind the door.” Boss Qian scratched his head. “Caution costs nothing. If something is there, perhaps this will persuade it to leave me alone.”

“You have a point.” Shaking his head, Chen Ge entered. By now, he seemed more familiar with the workshop than its owner. He gathered the necessary tools and went into storage. “Some of these materials will expire if you don’t use them. The place looks exactly as it did when I left. Have you had no business at all?”

“Business is fine.” Boss Qian followed him into storage and helped gather supplies. “I just finished researching the adult-doll market. Demand is booming. We could specialize in custom orders.”

“We’ll discuss it later.” Chen Ge dismissed the suggestion. Once the materials were ready, he recalled the repeatedly altered face of Patient No. 2 and produced a rough model within minutes.

“Running a Haunted House wastes your talent,” Boss Qian sighed. Ignoring him, Chen Ge concentrated on the clay and soon completed the woman’s face. Insane or not, she had been extraordinarily beautiful.

“But something is missing.” Chen Ge held the model for inspection before ruining it.

“Don’t!” Boss Qian cried out. “At least give it to me to show the customer!”

“This isn’t right,” Chen Ge murmured, beginning again. The second face conveyed sickness and madness. “Still wrong. Her madness carried pain.”

He started over, only to find the next face lacked vitality. The cycle repeated until Boss Qian grew numb to it, watching with mournful eyes while humming a sad ballad.

“What am I missing?” Recalling the description of his Dollmaker talent, Chen Ge conceived a daring idea. “Xu Yin trapped the woman’s lingering spirit in the tape. Perhaps he can release it into the mannequin. The woman herself is still alive, and the black phone describes a living doll as being based on a living person. What would happen if I placed her lingering spirit inside a doll made in her image?”

He stared at the clay in his hands, imagining the possibilities. The woman had participated in multiple murders. Even an insanity defense would not soon return her to freedom.

“I’ll have to rely on myself.” He resumed sculpting. “She underwent many surgeries. Each feature is beautiful in isolation, but together they produce something uncanny.”

Chen Ge dismantled the face, sculpted every feature separately, then joined them together. When he attached the final piece, the result was miraculous: a perfect likeness, down to the haunting expression. At last, he was satisfied.

“The features are separate pieces connected with steel wire. The face won’t break as easily this way.”

It could still split apart if a visitor came too close. Chen Ge chuckled as he imagined their reaction.

Before 9 a.m., Chen Ge completed five mannequins modeled after the woman, Xu Tong, Xiong Qing, the one-armed patient, and the tenacious nurse. Given time, he wanted to recreate the entire Third Sick Hall, patients and doctors alike.

“Now I have the characters. Add the proper props, and each mannequin becomes its own horror story.”

The filling needed time to set, so Chen Ge said goodbye to Boss Qian and left.

Chen Ge reached the Haunted House at 9 a.m. and opened for the day. As New Century Park’s gates admitted the first crowd, a substantial number headed straight for his attraction.

Uncle Xu noticed as well. From one perspective, the Haunted House had become the park’s leading attraction.

“Uncle Xu, you’re here. This is perfect; I was just looking for you.”

“Need help selling tickets? I’m free.” Uncle Xu moved naturally to the entrance. A rare smile appeared as he surveyed the long line.

Chen Ge waved him over. “I want to build a rest area beside the Haunted House. We can’t leave visitors standing in line all day.”

“No problem. Director Luo specifically ordered us to support you for the next two months.”

“I should still speak with Director Luo personally.” Chen Ge was planning for more than a simple rest area.

“He’ll be in his office around noon. See him then.” Uncle Xu assigned tasks over his radio. Soon a park van arrived, and several workers unloaded benches and canopy panels for a temporary shelter beside the Haunted House.

“These are left over from past park events. We’ll use them for now. You’ll have to discuss the permanent rest area—its size and everything else—with Director Luo.”

“Understood.”

Uncle Xu and the workers organized the queue. Most visitors waited patiently, but a large young man pushed through them toward Chen Ge.

“Wang Hailong? Why is he here?” Fearing something had happened to Wang Shenglong, Chen Ge hurried forward. “Did the boy finally break his silence?”
